title: On Measuring Social Biases in Sentence Encoders

bias_targets.methodology: Using the Sentence Encoder Association Test (SEAT) to measure the cosine similarity between sentence vectors of semantically bleached templates containing European American vs. African American names and templates containing pleasant vs. unpleasant attribute terms.

Applying SEAT to test implicit associations between male and female identifiers and attributes such as career/family, math/art, and science/art. It also tests a 'double bind' evaluating associations of female and male names with competence and likability in professional scenarios.

Evaluating the 'angry black woman' stereotype using SEAT by measuring the association strength between sentence templates containing black-identifying vs. white-identifying female names and templates containing stereotypical adjectives vs. their antonyms.
